observation.visible_scene: A calm coastal scene at twilight (sunset or sunrise). The lower half of the frame is a wet, glassy sand flat that acts as a mirror, reflecting the sky and clouds. On the right is a rocky pebble beach leading to a dark conifer treeline, with a small light-colored building at the far right edge. The upper half is a layered, broken cloud deck with a warm orange-yellow glow along the left/center horizon and a faint distant shoreline on the left. Several small stones and shell fragments sit motionless in the shallow water in the foreground.
visible_changes: The cloud formations overhead drift and deform very slightly from frame to frame, with the central dark cloud mass and the upper-right streaks shifting a small amount.

The warm glow at the horizon intensifies over the excerpt: a small bright sun point near the center-left horizon becomes more distinct, and the orange/pink tones in both the sky and its reflection grow stronger.
The wet-sand reflection mirrors these sky changes, gaining warmer color and a brighter streak as the excerpt progresses.
The foreground rocks, the treeline, the building, and the rocky beach on the right remain fixed in position, indicating a static (tripod) camera with no pan or zoom.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether this short real-time excerpt is part of a longer time-lapse or a continuous real-time shot.
The sun's exact position and behavior before and after the 2.67-second window.
Any wind speed or cloud motion that would be evident over a longer duration.
uncertain_details: The precise direction and speed of cloud drift are hard to confirm over such a short interval; the apparent motion is subtle.
It is uncertain whether the brightening is due to the sun emerging from behind cloud or simply to increasing light intensity at the horizon.
Minor pixel-level shifts could be compression artifacts rather than true motion.
